diagrams.alt: Coordinate axes with the x-axis from -3 to 7 and the y-axis from -4 to 6, on a 1-unit grid. Point A is at (-2, 5), to the left of the y-axis, and point B is at (6, -3), to the right of the y-axis and below the x-axis. The segment AB is drawn and crosses the y-axis.
diagrams.solutionAlt: In step 3 the point P where AB crosses the y-axis is marked at (0, 3); it divides AB in the ratio 1 : 3.

hints: Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0.
Let the ratio be \(k : 1\) and use the x-coordinate in the section formula.

solution.modelAnswer: Let \(P\) divide \(AB\) in the ratio \(k : 1\). Since \(P\) is on the y-axis, its x-coordinate is 0: \(\frac{6k - 2}{k + 1} = 0 \Rightarrow k = \tfrac{1}{3}\). So \(AP : PB = 1 : 3\). Then \(y = \frac{1(-3) + 3(5)}{1 + 3} = \frac{12}{4} = 3\), so \(P = (0, 3)\).

steps.title: Set up the section formula
steps.explanation: Let \(P\) divide \(AB\) in the ratio \(k : 1\), with \(A(-2, 5)\) as the first point and \(B(6, -3)\) as the second.
steps.rule: Section formula: \(\left(\frac{m x_2 + n x_1}{m + n}, \frac{m y_2 + n y_1}{m + n}\right)\)

steps.title: Use x = 0 on the y-axis
steps.explanation: \(P\) lies on the y-axis, so its x-coordinate is 0. Solving gives \(k = \tfrac{1}{3}\), so the ratio \(k : 1 = \tfrac{1}{3} : 1 = 1 : 3\).
steps.reason: The ratio is found from the coordinate whose value we know.

steps.title: Find the y-coordinate
steps.explanation: Substitute \(m : n = 1 : 3\) into the y-part of the section formula. The x-coordinate is 0 as already used.

commonMistakes: Setting the y-coordinate equal to 0 (that is the condition for the x-axis, not the y-axis).
Swapping the weights: computing \(\frac{1 \times 5 + 3 \times (-3)}{4} = -1\) instead of \(\frac{1 \times (-3) + 3 \times 5}{4}\).
Writing the ratio as \(3 : 1\) after finding \(k = \tfrac{1}{3}\).

alternativeMethods.title: Equation of the line
alternativeMethods.description: The slope of \(AB\) is \(\frac{-3 - 5}{6 - (-2)} = -1\), so the line is \(y = -x + 3\). It meets the y-axis at \((0, 3)\). Then the ratio is \(AP : PB = (0 - (-2)) : (6 - 0) = 2 : 6 = 1 : 3\), using the x-distances.

criteria.description: Uses the section formula with the condition x = 0
acceptedAlternatives: Equation of AB found and x = 0 substituted

criteria.partialCreditRules: Follow-through from an incorrect ratio if the substitution is carried out correctly.

questions.authorNotes: Diagram drawn to scale on a 1-unit grid; AB lies on y = 3 − x. Answer key is null because the answer is a ratio and a point. Figure has no grid or axis ticks, so the crossing point cannot be read off the figure; it is drawn to scale.

content.stem: The vertices of triangle \(PQR\) are \(P(5, -1)\), \(Q(-3, 4)\) and \(R(k, 3)\). The centroid of triangle \(PQR\) lies on the y-axis. Find the value of \(k\).

hints: What is the x-coordinate of any point on the y-axis?

solution.modelAnswer: The x-coordinate of the centroid is \(\frac{5 + (-3) + k}{3} = \frac{2 + k}{3}\). It lies on the y-axis, so \(\frac{2 + k}{3} = 0\), giving \(k = -2\).

steps.title: x-coordinate of the centroid
steps.explanation: The centroid's x-coordinate is the average of the three x-coordinates.

steps.title: Use the y-axis condition
steps.explanation: Points on the y-axis have x-coordinate 0. (As a check, the centroid is then \((0, 2)\).)

commonMistakes: Setting the y-coordinate of the centroid to 0 (the x-axis condition).
Dividing by 2 instead of 3, as if finding a mid-point.

criteria.description: Writes the centroid x-coordinate and equates it to 0
